title: Signal runbook daily log — Nov 20 2026 (Aziz)
body:
06:40 — pre-shift: quick skim of alerts, nothing noisy. coffee. set status to available.

07:05 — page: high 95th p99 latency on hosted text-gen in us-west-2. Alert: token-generation-latency > 1200ms for 5m.
  - first look: grafana dashboard (link above) shows a spike in small requests with low batch sizes. KV-cache hit rate dropped from ~98% to ~14% around 06:58.
  - pages: paged infra-oncall then model-serving team (Diego).

07:12 — triage notes:
  - hypothesis: cache eviction storm from rolling rollout + unusually large number of short-context requests (webchat clients).
  - quick checks:
    * kubectl get pods -n serving | grep qmodel  -> a couple of pods OOMKilled earlier (see pod logs), restart succeeded.
    * checked deploy rollout history for model-v2.3.1 -> canary was 06:45, ~30% traffic.

07:25 — mitigation actions (short term):
  - scaled up serving pool by +2 instances (manual) to absorb backlog (aziz).
  - increased cache TTL to 45s on the canary route (temporary flag flip).
  - activated fallback model r-v2-small for the heaviest tail of requests (auto-route policy set).
  - notified traffic-shaping to throttle noisy client id: webchat-frontend-3 (Marta to follow).

07:40 — immediate impact: KV hit rate recovering to ~70%, p95 down to ~420ms, p99 trending down but still elevated. No user-visible errors. Monitoring hook set: page if p99 > 900ms for 10m.

08:10 — root-cause sketch (rough):
  - simultaneous canary rollout + eviction of per-request prefix cache caused heavy recompute.
  - OOMKilled pods earlier indicate memory pressure on a subset of nodes; suspected incorrect OOM buffer setting in the autoscaler config (compare to stable pool).
  - missing defensive backpressure in the ingress path: small requests from webchat client created many tiny batches, no prefetch.

08:20 — runbook gaps observed (actionable):
  1) cache-rollout step missing explicit TTL override when enabling canary (probable root of TTL reset) — TODO (owner: Az): file runbook PR to add TTL check + fail-safe.
  2) autoscaler oom-threshold for model pods differs between dedicated/stable pools — TODO (owner: Diego): sync autoscaler policy and add unit test.
  3) ingress throttling rule absent for repeat small-context clients — TODO (owner: Marta): suggest rate-limit + aggregation.
  4) no automated canary rollback on sustained p99 degradation (only manual) — TODO (owner: eng-sre lead): design auto-rollback policy.

09:00 — quieter, started compiling incident timeline for postmortem draft. Noting what to capture:
  - timeline of deploys (canary 06:45), pod OOMs (06:50), cache eviction spike (06:58), remediation actions (07:25).
  - telemetry snapshots (before/after) have to be attached from grafana & logs (grab dashboards and export).

09:15 — quick commands run (notes to self):
  - kubectl -n serving get events --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 50 > /tmp/evt-tail.txt
  - gzcat /var/log/pods/qmodel-*/qmodel-*-stderr.log.gz | head -n 200 > /tmp/pod-stderr-snippet.txt
  - curl "https://api.redwood.ai/debug/cache-status?route=canary" -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEBUG_TOKEN" > /tmp/canary-cache.json

09:40 — followups issued (immediate):
  - JIRA-3421: "Investigate OOM pattern in canary nodes" -> assigned Diego, P0, due 2026-11-24.
  - JIRA-3440: "Runbook: add TTL safety check for cache rollout" -> assigned Az, P1, due 2026-11-22.
  - Slack @#model-serving pinned note: summary + links + ask for any other deploys at ~06:40 window.

10:05 — handover prep: pack concise bullet list for next oncall and SRE rotation. Include what to watch and how to remediate.
  - watch: p99 token-latency, kv-cache-hit-rate, OOMKills on model pods.
  - quick remediations: scale serving pool + bump TTL + switch to fallback model route.
  - important links: grafana (cache metrics), deploy history, pod logs (path pinned above).

10:30 — personal todo (post-shift):
  - draft postmortem skeleton in confluence (Az) — include attach telemetry and timeline.
  - open runbook PR adding TTL check + sample test (Az).
  - add regression alert that triggers on gradual cache-hit drop across multiple routes (SRE).
  - schedule short sync with model-serving team to discuss release gating (Marta + Diego + Az) — aim for 11/23.

Open questions / notes to self:
  - Why did pods OOM at that time specifically? Was there an external spike in token length or a memory leak in v2.3.1? Need heap/alloc traces if possible.
  - Should we add a canary memory metric to the autoscaler as a guardrail?

Handoff summary (to next oncall):
  - incident contained, no customer-facing errors observed, mitigations applied (scale + ttl bump + fallback).
  - primary followups: JIRA-3421 (OOM investigation), JIRA-3440 (runbook TTL safety), scheduled sync 11/23.
  - contact: Diego (model-serving), Marta (ingress/traffic), Az (SRE lead on followups).

Quick wins for future shifts (brainstorm):
  - add canary-deploy checklist in CI that validates cache TTL & mem limits before traffic shift.
  - create a synthetic profile of small-context high-frequency requests to test canary effects.
  - implement auto-rollbacks when p99 > threshold for N minutes.

End-of-shift notes (11:55): left handoff message in #oncall and pinned the key logs to the incident channel. Going offline but will be available on mobile for 30m if any flash regressions.

---

Misc scratch scraps (noise I kept):
  - idea: try a small local harness to reproduce KV churn by rapidly toggling the TTL flag and hitting the canary endpoint with 40 tps small requests.
  - mental note: check if dedicated pool had a different VM SKU that caused memory fragmentation.
  - leave the commands I ran in /tmp and an archive in S3 (s3://redwood-debug/aziz/2026-11-20/) — attach in confluence later.
notes: This is a personal oncall scratchpad used for running log of pages, quick mitigation steps and a checklist of followups to convert into formal tickets and a postmortem. Kept intentionally informal.
